metadata.goal: Analyze how the vessel navigates within a structured shipping corridor and identify any route-following, crossing, or recovery behaviors that distinguish the voyage.
metadata.header: Vessel Route Following, Recovery, and Crossing Behavior
metadata.dataset_description: The main table contains one target cargo-vessel voyage plus surrounding commercial AIS-like traffic defining a structured northbound lane and expected turn branch. It provides local and geographic coordinates, timestamp, course, speed, traffic role, and movement phase.

insight_list.insight: The vessel follows the dominant traffic lane closely for most of the voyage, with its course remaining well aligned with the surrounding commercial traffic flow.

plot.title: Lane Following and Course Alignment
plot.description: The map compares the target vessel with surrounding commercial tracks, while the course panel shows the target vessel's lane-following segment.

insight_list.question: For which portion of the voyage does the vessel remain aligned with the dominant traffic lane and surrounding commercial traffic?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Inspect the event sequence, locations, and operating intervals together rather than treating each trip independently.

insight_list.insight: The vessel continues beyond the typical turning point without making the expected course change, then performs a pronounced corrective turn to rejoin the established shipping route.

plot.title: Missed Turn and Corrective Recovery
plot.description: The expected turn branch is dashed; the target vessel's overshoot and corrective segment are shown separately.

insight_list.question: Does the vessel make the expected turn at the usual point, and if not, how does it recover?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Inspect the event sequence, locations, and operating intervals together rather than treating each trip independently.

insight_list.insight: Rather than travelling along the dominant traffic corridor, the vessel crosses the main shipping flow at a large angle, producing a movement pattern clearly different from ordinary lane-following traffic.

plot.title: Large-Angle Crossing of the Main Flow
plot.description: The red target-vessel segment is shown against the gray northbound commercial traffic lanes.

insight_list.question: Does any part of the target vessel's voyage cross the dominant shipping flow rather than follow it?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Inspect the event sequence, locations, and operating intervals together rather than treating each trip independently.
insight_list.code:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
d=df.copy(); q=d[(d.traffic_role.eq('target_vessel')) & (d.movement_phase.eq('crossing_flow'))]; print(q[['x_km','y_km','cog']].describe()); plt.plot(q.x_km,q.y_km,color='red'); plt.show()

insights: The vessel follows the dominant traffic lane closely for most of the voyage, with its course remaining well aligned with the surrounding commercial traffic flow.
The vessel continues beyond the typical turning point without making the expected course change, then performs a pronounced corrective turn to rejoin the established shipping route.

Rather than travelling along the dominant traffic corridor, the vessel crosses the main shipping flow at a large angle, producing a movement pattern clearly different from ordinary lane-following traffic.
summary: The target vessel follows the principal commercial lane for much of the voyage, but misses an expected turn, executes a visible corrective maneuver to rejoin the established branch, and later crosses the principal traffic flow at a large angle. These three phases distinguish it from ordinary lane-following traffic.
